producer_report.summary: `athena drain` now follows `athena plan`'s order when groups are involved. The full suite, fmt, clippy, the policy scan and the mirrors test all pass. I did not run the new tests against the old code. Root cause: `Plan::build_with` built groups wave by wave with greedy joining. A lower-priority item could sit in an earlier group than a higher-priority one that clashed with an earlier item, and drain works groups in sequence. The wave loop now only fixes the order (best effective priority, then rung, then age). A new `groups_in_order` then builds the groups from that order. An item joins the last group if it is path-disjoint with all members and depends on none of them. Otherwise it opens a new group. So the flattened groups equal `Plan::order`, and a group is never before the group of anything it depends on. With one job at a time, drain dispatches exactly in plan order. `batches_for` and the `build_improving` regrouping are unchanged. I added a comment in `build_improving` saying the regrouping keeps the flattened groups equal to the moved order. Docs are updated in plan.rs and drain.rs. Two existing plan tests changed their group expectations. The `athena plan` display test in `crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs` now expects `group 1     urgent, a` and `group 2     b`. New tests: two in plan.rs and two in drain.rs, which use a `with_priority` builder and a `started()` helper on the `World` fixture. CHANGELOG.md has an entry under Unreleased/Fixed.

criteria_check.criterion: A new test (in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs tests, via `cargo test`) plans a normal item and an urgent item with disjoint touched paths and no dependency, and shows drain with max_concurrency 1 dispatches the urgent item first.
criteria_check.evidence: Added `with_one_job_at_a_time_an_urgent_item_starts_before_an_older_disjoint_normal_one` in drain.rs read_ahead_tests. It queues normal n, then urgent u, with disjoint paths. It runs `concurrent(&world, 1)` and asserts started == [u, n] and report.plan_groups.concat() == [u, n]. I also added `..._drain_dispatches_exactly_in_plan_order_when_groups_form`, the 2026-10-27 shape (u1 and u2 clash, n is a dependency of u4, u3 urgent), which expects [u1,u2,n,u3,u4]. Both pass under `cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --lib drain::`. I did not run either test against the old code. By hand, the old grouping would start u1, n, u3, u2, u4 for the second test.

criteria_check.criterion: A new test in plan.rs (`cargo test -p athena-core`) shows a dependency's group comes before its dependent's group whatever their priorities, including a normal-priority dependency of an urgent item and a case where the dependent has a higher priority than its dependency.

It covers normal base with urgent dependent, urgent base with low dependent, normal base with high dependent beside an urgent item, and low base with low dependent beside an urgent item. For each case it asserts base is before dependent in the order and in group index, and that groups.concat() == order. It passes in `cargo test -p athena-core --lib plan::`.

criteria_check.criterion: A new plan.rs test shows that for a mixed plan the flattened Plan::groups equals Plan::order, and no later group holds an item of higher priority than an earlier group unless a dependency explains it.
criteria_check.evidence: Added `groups_flatten_to_the_order_and_a_later_group_never_outranks_an_earlier_one_without_a_dependency`. It uses an 8-item mixed plan. It pins the order [u1,u2,n,u3,u4,h,m,l] and the groups [[u1],[u2,n,u3],[u4,h,m,l]]. It repeats the flatten and inversion checks for `build_capped`, and checks flatten for `build_improving` with a moved steward request. It passes.

open_issues: Parallel breadth changes: an item that clashes with an earlier one now opens a new group, and later disjoint items join that group instead of an earlier one. Disjoint items of different priorities can also share a group. Both are documented in the `build_with` doc and the CHANGELOG entry. Existing group-size tests still pass.
I did not run the new drain and plan tests against the old grouping code. The claim that they fail there rests on tracing the old greedy loop by hand.
learnings: The producer shell hook rejects grep, rg, tail, redirections and command substitution; use Grep/Read and plain cargo commands. A foreground cargo call fails with exit 75 ('no build slot free') while another cargo run holds the slot, so retrying works.
Within a wave the ready items never depend on each other, so joining only the last group and checking `depends_on` against its members is enough to keep groups after their dependencies.
`athena plan` group lines are asserted by needle in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs; only the one display test needed new needles.
